🔍 Computer vision

Convolution

In simple words

Sliding a small grid of numbers (a filter) across a picture to find patterns such as edges.

A way of finding patterns in a picture: a small grid of numbers, called a filter, slides over the image. At every spot it multiplies the pixels under it by its own numbers and adds the results up. Where the pattern it looks for is, for example an edge, the result is large.

Example. The blur and sharpen effects in a photo editor are convolutions with simple filters. A filter that compares each pixel's left and right neighbours lights up vertical edges.

Related words

  • PixelOne tiny square of a digital picture, stored as numbers that say how bright it is or what colour it has.
  • Convolutional neural network (CNN)A neural network for pictures whose layers use convolutions to find patterns, from edges up to whole objects.
